why: A (universe 0; the example theorems have no universe) has eleven conjuncts. remark_10_5_5: for every k, [W ←1 W →Inv W] and [1_W] over ℤ/3 × ℝ ⇉ ℝ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with the same |[D]|, different base classes, and [Inv] ≠ [1]. The others are pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id (the positive half for this example only), the example lemmas z3InvHom_mem_equivalences, orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom and base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom, the IsotropyRel invariant and its lemmas, and remark_10_5_3. B = (1) ¬∀ f f' generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with the same square |𝒟| (both orbit maps), f = f'; and (2) for all such pairs, [D]_* = [D']_* and [D]^* = [D']^* on section functors. A_to_B: (1) from A's remark_10_5_5 at k = 0, with base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom for the base orbit maps. (2) is NOT in A: A has the positive half only for the example. The general statement is the last part of GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4 (item V10_59, a non-item lemma here), which proves (2) outright rather than from the hypothesis. B_to_A: pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id comes from B (2). B (1) is a non-constructive ¬∀ that does not name the example, so remark_10_5_5 and the example lemmas cannot come from B; neither can the general IsotropyRel lemmas or remark_10_5_3. They are re-proved outright by copying the project's proofs from non-item lemmas (isMap_z3Inv, isStrongBundleEquivalence_of_inverse, the isotropyConj helpers, EPLoc.homMk_eq_homMk_iff, EPLoc.theorem_10_3_10). So the two sides agree on the remark's content, but the item's own decls contain the positive half only through the example; the general positive half is in V10_59's theorem_10_5_4, as the project's docstring says ('Its last part is the positive half of Remark 10.5.5').
